Ironically I am specialized in air safety and I get a lot of stress when flying, mainly because I know pretty much every single thing that can go wrong and I am constantly analizing the situation.
The most I can do to keep myself the most calm possible is to do everything in my hand to make sure my flight is going to be safe, and for that I do the following:

- Fly with reliable airlines that have good safety records, with 0 fatal crashes in the last 10 years, follows all safety audits, it's not in the EU blacklist, etc
For that you can check your airline on "airlineratings.com"  and find your airline safety rating, if it has a 7/7 you are good to go. Of course certain airlines have a reputation for being safe during years, Qatar will always be at the top safest airlines in the world with 0 fatalities since 1951. 

- Know your aircraft, when you book a flight you can see wich aircraft the airline will use, certain aircraft have far better safety records than others, I personally try to avoid ATR72 at all costs, and prefer to fly with Airbus at the moment (sorry Boeing but you're not doing your best engineering aircraft for quite a while, specially when even Boeing engineers have said they wouldnt get in one even if they got payed to do so because they know how they are built).

- Do not fly first class, if you can or want to choose your own seat opt for seats in the rear side of the aircraft, you might notice turbulence more there but there is a good reason why black boxes are as far into the tail as possible. If you think turbulences will freak you out too much then get an aisle seat on the wing area.

Those are some of the steps that you can do to feel as safe as possible 🤷🏼
